book.satiscraftory.name: Satiscraftory Field Guide
book.satiscraftory.landing: Build your first conveyor, choose a belt tier, and connect your production lines.$(br2)Start with $(l:satiscraftory:basics/first_belt)Your First Belt$(/l), or browse the tier recipes and routing blocks.
gui.satiscraftory.template_hint: Click with an item or drag from JEI. Right-click to clear.
gui.satiscraftory.no_recipes_2: No recipes using up to two ingredients
gui.satiscraftory.no_recipes_4: No recipes using up to four ingredients
gui.satiscraftory.filter_set_hint: Click with an item or drag from JEI.
tip.satiscraftory.first_belt: Start with two chests. Hold a belt and sneak-right-click the source face, then the destination face.
tip.satiscraftory.exact_face: Sneak while aiming at an inventory to highlight the exact face the belt will use.
tip.satiscraftory.stacked_connections: Stack your chests directly above each other. Sneak-click their faces to attach belts without support blocks underneath.
tip.satiscraftory.route_modes: Press Tab during a belt preview to switch between rounded right angles and a flowing spline. Your choice is remembered.
tip.satiscraftory.cancel_preview: Changed your mind about a belt route? Right-click empty air to cancel the preview.
tip.satiscraftory.section_length: One belt item places a whole section, up to 16 blocks along the route. Join sections at their ends for longer runs.
tip.satiscraftory.belt_ports: Extend a line from an open end. A belt's side is a railing, even when the shortcut would be extremely convenient.
tip.satiscraftory.vertical_routes: Both route modes can climb and descend. Run an overhead supply line to keep the floor clear.
tip.satiscraftory.pick_belt: Use Pick Block anywhere along a belt to grab its tier. There's no need to find the block that anchors it.
tip.satiscraftory.pick_cargo: Right-click cargo to lift it off the belt. If your inventory is full, the item keeps its place.
tip.satiscraftory.mine_section: Hold left click anywhere on a belt to mine that section. A pickaxe is fastest, and the belt drops where you broke it.
tip.satiscraftory.recover_cargo: Breaking a loaded belt drops cargo along the route. Empty it first if you don't feel like walking the entire line.
tip.satiscraftory.tier_swap: Hold a different belt tier and right-click the yellow outline to swap tiers in place. The route and cargo stay put.
tip.satiscraftory.belt_recipe: Mk.1 belts use planks and copper ingots. Each higher tier uses one belt from the previous tier in the center of its recipe.
tip.satiscraftory.find_bottleneck: Before upgrading an entire line, check the destination. A faster belt delivers items to a full chest at exactly the same rate.
tip.satiscraftory.trace_a_jam: Trace a jam from the destination backward. Check storage space, machine power, and whether the last belt meets the right port.
tip.satiscraftory.test_parcel: Send one cheap item through a new line before loading the source chest. A cobblestone is cheaper than an incident report.
tip.satiscraftory.splitter_ports: A Splitter's input faces you when placed. It takes turns sending items to the other three sides and skips blocked outputs.
tip.satiscraftory.merger_ports: A Merger's output faces away from you when placed. Give the combined line enough speed to keep up with its inputs.
tip.satiscraftory.convert_router: Put a Splitter alone in a crafting grid to turn it into a Merger. The reverse recipe works the same way.
tip.satiscraftory.smart_orientation: On a Smart Splitter, left and right are from the input's point of view, looking in the direction items travel.
tip.satiscraftory.overflow_chest: Send a Smart Splitter's Overflow side to a spare chest. Items go there when no matching regular output can accept them.
tip.satiscraftory.smart_filters: A Smart Splitter can hold nine filter templates per output. Whitelist lets listed items through. Blacklist keeps them out.
tip.satiscraftory.empty_whitelist: An empty Smart Splitter whitelist admits nothing. Handy for closing one lane while you work on it.
tip.satiscraftory.ghost_filter: Click a Smart Splitter filter slot with a carried item or drag one from JEI. Click with an empty cursor to clear it.
tip.satiscraftory.smelter_power: Connect RF to any of the Smelter's four copper faces. The furnace face takes items and the opposite face sends them out.
tip.satiscraftory.smelter_passthrough: The Smelter spends 1,000 RF per smelted item. Items with no furnace recipe pass through unchanged for free.
tip.satiscraftory.machine_templates: Set a crafting machine's Template to what you want it to make. Pick a recipe row if there are several ways to make it.
tip.satiscraftory.machine_capacity: Pick your crafter by distinct ingredient types: one for a Constructor, up to two for an Assembler, and up to four for a Manufacturer.
tip.satiscraftory.machine_output: The dropper face is a crafting machine's output. The other faces can accept ingredients or RF.
tip.satiscraftory.machine_buffers: Assemblers and Manufacturers buffer up to two crafts' worth of each ingredient. Fill the missing ingredient before adding more of the others.
tip.satiscraftory.cake_buckets: A Manufacturer can make cake. Plan a return trip for the empty milk buckets that come out with it.
tip.satiscraftory.field_guide: With Patchouli installed, craft the Satiscraftory Field Guide from a book, a copper ingot, and yellow dye.
tip.satiscraftory.safety_footbridge: Belts can cross a ravine. You can walk through them, so budget for a separate bridge.
tip.satiscraftory.temporary_line: Put a sign over your temporary belt. It helps identify the original temporary belt after the second temporary belt has been built around it.
tip.satiscraftory.department_loop: Run one potato around a belt loop and label it Quality Control. If it comes back, the inspection was brief but conclusive.
